title: The normalized principal quotient unit detects actual integral derived completeness
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and Y a scheme. Set R to the actual completed integral commutative ring sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and t to the actual constant uniformizer section [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement]. Let C be any universal principal quotient completion Model(R,t), including its counit, K-flat computation, strict augmentation with the quotient product coordinate and zero shifted coordinate, and compatible natural derived unit [def-pur-principal-quotient-completion-model]. For every K in the unbounded derived category of the actual completed-coefficient module sheaves, IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted(l,E,Y,K) [def-weil-derived-complete] holds if and only if C.unit at K is an isomorphism. No equality between the site and coefficient universes is assumed.

proof.text: Restrict the ring and modules along the canonical equivalence from the small model in the coefficient universe. This is an exact equivalence, so it preserves products and derived products. Transport scalar multiplication and the actual quotient maps. The normalized sheafification comparison ensures that sectionwise tensor maps retain their pure-tensor formulas.

The completed exact sequence identifies the cokernel of t^(n+1) with the actual constant residue module, preserving its quotient map and transitions. Tensor the comparison with a flat-term K-flat representative. Exact countable products preserve the resulting quasi-isomorphisms and the signed Roos cone, and preserve the zero shifted-coordinate unit.

Apply the regular quotient completion unit criterion on the small model. Its distinguished triangle with the prescribed quotient components transports to exactly the defining derived-limit triangle of actual integral derived completeness. Refine to a flat-term K-flat resolution and transport along its derived isomorphism. The auxiliary finite-field datum changes none of the rings or maps; choose characteristic 2 or 3 different from l.

Universal left-derived uniqueness compares the given Model with this normalized quotient construction. On K-flat representatives, the two cone coordinates determine the augmentation and its unit comparison. The localization universal property extends the resulting unit equation to all derived objects. Isomorphism of those unit maps transports the criterion to the supplied Model.

lean.statement:
theorem completedIntegralPrincipalUnitCriterion
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t})
    (C : @PrincipalQuotientCompletion.Model.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1) + 1}
      Y.ProEt inferInstance (essentiallySmallSelf.{u} _)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) inferInstance
      (integralCoefficientAbSheafify.{t, u} Y)
      (integralCoefficientAbLocallyBijective.{t, u} Y)
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E Y)
      (integralTowerHasDerivedCategory l E Y)
      (PrincipalKoszulStrictReplacement.uniformizer l E Y)) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y),
      IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E Y K ↔ IsIso (C.unit.app K)
